The body of A gets it right; the epigraph blurs the section's own first-birth/second-birth distinction. Use B's epigraph wording ('began human life conceived of the Holy Ghost').

(A) COL 66.1 is misfiled under 'The laver — cleansing joined to power.' The verified paragraph is about GROWTH after conversion ('The plant grows by receiving...'), not the washing; A's own gloss concedes 'after the birth, growth runs by the same law.' B's dedicated 'Not by might — the power named and offered' block (Zech. 4:6 → COL 66.1 → Acts 1:8) is the honest placement.
(B) Block heading claims John 3:3-7 but v. 4 is silently dropped. A's John 3:4 bullet ('Nicodemus's bewilderment measures the demand') is verified and should be restored so the range is honest.

(B) In the DEFINITION, _SC 75.2_ is cited against the John 6:57 hand-over clause; the verified SC 75.2 quotes John 5:19 and 14:10, not 6:57. Re-anchor SC 75.2 to the 'can do nothing of himself / Father that dwelleth in me' clause (as A does) and let John 6:57 stand alone or with DA 363.1.

(BOTH / ground-truth pack) The witness-pack tail for DA 363.1 — 'Receiving life from God, He imparted life to men' — is NOT verbatim. The actual paragraph reads: 'Through continual communion He received life from God, that He might impart life to the world. His experience is to be ours.' B uses the tail only as unquoted gloss (acceptable); the synthesizer must NOT promote it to a quotation. Better: quote the verified closing sentence 'His experience is to be ours' — the strongest hand-over line in the paragraph, and neither draft uses it.
(B) Minor wording: 'the nature He bore is walked in "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"' — 'is walked in' is clumsy; reword to A's '(see ...)' form.

(BOTH) Neither draft makes the by-faith mechanism explicit. The ground-truth uncertainties note Heb. 5:8-9 and Gal. 2:20 were verified and held in reserve for exactly this; if the synthesizer wants the 'lived by faith / we live by His faith' link stated, those are the only sanctioned additions — do not invent others.

(BOTH) The 'laver' label rests solely on the ground-truth symbol definition; neither draft anchors the sanctuary-laver typology in a text or Haskell witness. Acceptable as-is (the symbol def sanctions it), but the synthesizer should not add typological claims beyond the four receipts (Titus 3:5; Eph. 5:26; Eze. 36:25-27; Zech. 4:6).
bestOf: Use B's architecture as the skeleton: its seven-block progression (conception → childhood surrender → how He lived → new birth → laver → 'Not by might' power block → 'The result' block) is cleaner than A's, correctly separates COL 66.1/Zech 4:6/Acts 1:8 from the laver, and its DEFINITION paragraph (base it there, with the SC 75.2 anchor fixed) closes with the forward link to 'Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame,' giving the section an arc. Keep B's epigraph (theologically precise on 'conceived'). Pull from A: (1) the John 3:4 bullet — restores the claimed range and is the best gloss in either draft; (2) the Luke 1:35 'mark the two agents' gloss (sharper than B's equation form); (3) the Eze. 36:26 'transplant: stony heart out, heart of flesh in' gloss; (4) the DA 363.1 gloss 'power came by dependence, prayed for and received' (but per defects, consider adding the verified 'His experience is to be ours'); (5) all three of A's discussion questions — markedly more concrete and self-implicating than B's (A's Q1 'where in this week's decisions are you still living of your own self' and Q2 'which half have you been attempting alone' vs B's more abstract framings); (6) A's fuller 'Symbols carried' wording. Keep both drafts' shared elements as-is: the CHR 27.3 + DA 117.2 pairing with the consent-not-nature resolution, the inline + end symbol definitions (identical in substance), and the 1SM 226.2 → 2 Pet. 1:4 'partaker of the divine nature' bracket, which both execute well.
